title: Signed components, shared identities, and conditional resource compatibility
scope: Finite bipartite resource experiment, not chess attack-defense cancellation, chess legality, an engine, or an Elo test.
enumeration: Every binary incidence matrix A[d,t], graph integer bit d*4+t. Every demand mask 0..15, including empty. Conditions: none or disable one fixed labelled defender d. Uniform original graph weighting; condition and demand are known query context.
query: Is there an injective assignment from demanded targets to available adjacent defenders? Each defender serves at most one demanded target.
oracle: Enumerate every injective assignment/permutation of the available labelled defenders for the demanded targets. A query is feasible iff one assignment's required incidence bits are all present. Oracle uses graph bits, not transforms, Gram matrices, Hall summaries, or the experimental composition operator.

representations.name: counts_after
representations.meaning: All four per-target available-defender counts; energy-only baseline

representations.name: energy_after
representations.meaning: Per-target sum of squared signed Walsh coefficients divided by 4; expected information-equivalent to binary incidence counts

representations.name: signed_full_after
representations.meaning: All four signed Walsh coefficients for each target, with a fixed shared defender basis

representations.name: magnitude_full_after
representations.meaning: Absolute values of all four Walsh coefficients per target; discarded relative sign

representations.name: pooled_signed_after
representations.meaning: Sum of complete signed target vectors over demanded targets; target separation discarded

representations.name: counts_plus_pooled_after
representations.meaning: All per-target counts plus the pooled signed vector over demanded targets

representations.name: gram_after
representations.meaning: Upper triangle of A^T A after the condition, including diagonal counts

representations.name: gram_root
representations.meaning: Upper triangle of root A^T A; fixed labelled removal condition is supplied but source identities are absent

representations.name: independently_relabelled_full_after
representations.meaning: Each target independently renames its adjacent defenders to 0..count-1, then retains its full signed Walsh vector; demonstrates loss of cross-channel identity alignment

representations.name: incidence_after
representations.meaning: Complete available incidence, packed as n*4 bits

transform: Unnormalized 4x4 Sylvester Walsh-Hadamard H[f,d]=(-1)^popcount(f&d), zero-pad the 3-defender domain to four slots. For each target F_t=H*A_t. Signed components are exact integers. This is a reversible sum/difference change of basis, not a compression-size claim.
conditional_operator: Disable fixed defender d directly in the signed basis: F'_t=(I-h_d*h_d^T/4)*F_t, where h_d is column d of H. Check exact integer divisibility and compare against separately encoded available incidence.
direct_joint_operator: Represent compatible used-resource assignments by a multilinear polynomial with x_d^2=0. Walsh-transform its 2^n coefficient vector. A demanded target multiplies by sum_d A[d,t]*x_d. Precompute the transformed creation tensor C_f[k,l]=sum_d H[f,d]*(-1)^bit_d(k)*(delta(l,k)+delta(l,k xor 2^d)). Update z'=sum_f F_t[f]*C_f*z/8. Initial z is all ones; final z[0] is the number of injective assignments. Implementation keeps exact scaled integers and answers z[0]>0 without reconstructing incidence or calling the matching oracle.
operator_ablations: absolute coefficients interpreted by the same operator
three-frequency completion using a known unavailable/padded defender, otherwise zero-fill
completion_rule: If a known defender d is unavailable, A[d,t]=0 implies F_missing=-H[missing,d]*sum_kept H[f,d]*F[f]. For n=3, padded defender 3 is always known unavailable. For n=4, a removal condition supplies such a defender. Completion is not used when no zero component is known.
metrics: cases and oracle-positive count per domain/condition/demand
number/fraction of graphs in ambiguous groups
fixed representation bytes and observed log2(unique signatures)
actual direct-operator false positives/false negatives/negative outputs
exact matching count mismatch for full signed operator
CPU wall times recorded as diagnostic, no performance-gain claim
collision_method: Within each fixed domain, condition, and demand, group every graph by the representation. A mixed-label group is an information collision. Retain deterministic first graph pair as a reproducible witness. Do not infer different queries from the same key: query context remains fixed.
predeclared_worked_cases: Counts and complete demanded-vector pooling can share row/column margins while different source-target incidence changes matching.
Test a four-defender Gram collision built from the star-plus-unique and triangle-plus-empty incidence patterns, with target 3 duplicating target 0.
Test two row-permuted graphs under removal of the same labelled defender: unconditioned Gram equality need not preserve the conditional answer.
hypotheses: Counts/energies cannot generally answer joint resource compatibility.
A complete signed representation is sufficient only with shared identity alignment and a compatible joint operator; invertibility alone is not an algorithmic gain.
Pairwise Gram information may suffice on the smaller domain but lose higher intersections or fixed labels on the larger/conditional tasks; report whatever exhaustive results show.
Discarding a coefficient can be harmless when a declared boundary condition determines it, but a fixed zero-fill decoder need not exploit that fact.
The transformed compatibility operator may cost more than an ordinary small matching procedure; correctness and ambiguity, not speedup, are this experiment's primary outcomes.
execution: CPU only, one pinned core where available. NumPy exact integer arrays; record Python/NumPy versions, source SHA-256 and protocol SHA-256. Commit protocol first, then source before first measured run. Deterministic enumeration, no fit/MLP/training/search/gameplay. Commit compact JSON and report, not per-graph arrays.
